tells: 1. The laugh doesn't build: across the whole 1 s strip only the woman in the white sweater lifts a hand and two heads turn. Mouths stay closed and nobody's shoulders or torso move, so it reads as a cut to the next shot, not a reaction to a line (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, front tables)

2. The wide and the held frame are almost pose-identical: same head angles, same hands on tables, same back-row silhouettes. At living-room distance the room looks paused (club-1-wide.png vs club-6-held.png, whole frame)

3. The face close has a waxy, CG-plastic look: uniform sheen, a dark cut-out halo around the hair and shoulder edge against the DOF background, and dead, unfocused eyes on a half-open mouth that reads as speaking, not laughing (club-4-face.png, subject outline and eyes)

4. Lighting is a flat frontal fill on the front row. Faces get the same exposure as the shirts, with no key-to-fill ratio, no candle underlight or stage-spill falloff, and only weak rim separation from the back rows. The back crowd sits as an even grey-brown mush of identical-height standing figures (club-1-wide.png, front tables vs rows behind)

5. A hard black rectangle (a stage lip or speaker with no shading) cuts across the bottom centre, and the lower frame crushes to pure black with no detail, which looks like a missing mesh more than shadow (club-1-wide.png, bottom centre x≈330–550)

1. Behind the first two lit rows the auditorium is a wall of identical flat black cut-out silhouettes, all upright, the same height and evenly spaced. They read as cardboard, not people in the dark, and the jump in light from the lit rows to them is a cliff with no gradation (theatre-1-wide.png, theatre-6-held.png, upper half)

2. Front-row posture: bodies sit bolt upright with thighs barely bent, as if standing in front of the seats, with hands parked identically on knees. Several look stiff, like mannequins (theatre-1-wide.png, front row; theatre-3-mid.png, centre-right women)

3. Face close: overexposed, glossy plastic skin with no pores; a gaping mouth with a flat dark interior and a smeared tongue; eyes looking off-axis with no catchlight. It reads as a game character, not a laughing person (theatre-4-face.png, mouth and eyes)

4. The laugh is weak and staggered without building. Two or three mouths open at 12.6–12.8, the teal hoodie man looks down at his hands at 13.0, and the back row never moves (theatre-5-strip.png, bottom row)

5. The light has no motivation: the front rows are evenly lit as if by a softbox from the camera, while the visible practicals are tiny dots in the haze with no throw. The man in a cap at the right goes almost black and loses his head shape (theatre-2-mid.png, right edge; theatre-1-wide.png, top)

1. The DOF composite leaves dark halo rims around every in-focus subject, there is visible grain or dither on the skin, and the hair at the back of the head of the man in yellow is a streaky, comb-like smear (openmic-4-face.png, right side of the hair; openmic-6-held.png, outlines of all three foreground figures)

2. The crowd is packed into one overlapping clump. Shoulders and knees interpenetrate, and the front row perches forward on invisible stools with stiff, splayed legs (openmic-1-wide.png, centre front row, green-top woman and dark-hoodie woman)

3. The reaction is carried by two women while everyone else stays poker-faced. The yellow-shirt man's expression doesn't change across the 1 s, so the laugh doesn't feel like it spreads through the room (openmic-5-strip.png, all frames, left half)

4. Faces are smooth and mask-like under a flat warm wash. The eyes have no wet highlight, the smile on the yellow-shirt man is painted rather than muscular, and the half-lit faces in the second row look like cut-outs (openmic-4-face.png, eyes; openmic-3-mid.png, second row)

5. The wide is underexposed and muddy. The row of ceiling downlights doesn't actually light anyone below it, a bright flat panel at the left edge reads as an unlit card, and the back silhouettes are featureless (openmic-1-wide.png, top half and left edge)
